about: Which prop art (manifest.json in this folder) dresses each thing in data/locations, read by world/look/set_dressing.gd (docs/art/set_dressing.md). A location prop or container is looked up by its id in `ids` first, then by its `model` in `models`; with neither it uses the art of the same name as its model, else `container_default` for containers. A value is an art id, or {art, mount, scale} to override how it hangs, or null for an invisible spot (something already drawn, or a view). `on_wall` is the art used when the thing stands on a wall square (shelves against a wall). Doors take the first `doors.rules` entry whose words are in their id or label. `floors` gives a place its own ground texture; `low_cover.<place>` and `<place>_run` dress its '=' squares. An entry with `building: true` stands in for the whole house on its square (a windmill, a bell tower); `fade: true` fades a tall piece like the trees. `scales` sizes a piece wherever it stands (stairs fill their square); `fronts` gives furniture a front view that stands flat against a wall beside it. `rooms` gives a location's areas their own floor and wall by words in the area's name (a bathroom's tiles); `place_looks` overrides a whole place's floor, wall, difficult ground and `rock_walls` (cliffs instead of trees). `feet` is each standing piece's real height (a person is 6 ft; 1 unit = 5 ft): the piece is drawn at that size, and `feet` is the height of its picture at real size (low, deep things such as beds include the top you see from above). A piece wider than `big_width` units at that size (a cottage, a tent, a wagon) keeps its size whatever the room and clears the trees and the board's own scenery around it. `glows` are pieces drawn unshaded, giving light rather than taking it. `double_doors` are exit art drawn once across a doorway two squares wide (outside interiors: the keep's great doors). `rooms` applies to interiors and dungeons only; `outdoor_rooms` are the few rules for outdoor maps (jetties are planks).

models3d.about: 3D pieces from art/models (blender/models_3d.py, docs/art/models.md) that stand in for 2D art, by art id; a value can be {board theme: model, "*": model} (wooden stairs indoors, stone ones elsewhere) or a list of variants the board picks from by square (pines, boulders). Only the places listed use them ("*": everywhere, owner sign-off 2026-10-06). walls: a wall surface whose painted panelling gets 3D panels on every open face.

building_kit.about: Town houses from the building kit (art/models/kit, blender/building_kit.py, docs/art/building_kit.md): the style each place's houses are built in (its own, else its board theme's); a place or theme not named keeps the plain boxes. The house that holds a church's doors is built in the church style (stone, buttresses, lancets and a bell tower). cores: the house's wall behind the modules (a texture set, or none for a dark core where boards cover it). roofs: thatch or slate for small houses and for grand ones (grand_area squares or more). paints: the colours Vallaki's clapboard houses are painted, one per house.

interiors.about: Interiors: the style a place's rooms are built in, by the start of its id, else by board theme. A lone wall square inside a room is a pillar in that style (kit_pillar_<style>); every open face of a cut-away wall gets the style's coping along its top and, where no panelling does, its face module (kit_<style>_coping, kit_<style>_face). full_walls (W8, Modern look only): rooms get full-height walls that cut away toward the camera, height by style; ground: what lies outside the building by style, and outside: a place's own (its ground, how many storeys below it lies, its walls' height); a dungeon's outside is rock.

castle.about: Castle Ravenloft from outside (W19, CastleBuilder, Modern look only), by place: rect is the castle's part of the map [x, z, w, d] (its wall squares are the castle; walls outside it stay as they were); wall and keep are the curtain walls' and the keep's heights; keeps are rects of keep squares; blocks are more of the castle past the map's edge [x, z, w, d, height]; towers are round towers {at: [x, z] in squares, r, h, from (above 0 a turret rising out of the keep, below 0 a tower rising out of the drop), spire: cone, needle or none}; parapets are rects whose wall squares are a low wall (the cliff road's edge); heights are rects [x, z, w, d, height] of walls of their own height (a raised roof's parapet); cliffs false makes the void a drop off the castle's roofs, its masonry going down `below` under every square beside it instead of rock; bridges are rects of the squares that span the chasm (timbers under them, no cliffs).

clutter.about: Decals laid over floors and walls by rule (world/look/clutter.gd, docs/art/decals.md): per board theme, or per place by the start of its id. decals: decal ids or sheet names (art/textures/decals/manifest.json); on: floor, edge (beside a wall), difficult, boundary (beside rough ground: mud fringes where cobbles meet mud), wall or wall_foot (an open face of a wall); chance per square; size in world units; max per board; tint darkens or colours a mark; gloss makes it wet (puddles glint). A rule with scatter instead names kit models (blender/building_kit.py kit_scatter_*) strewn on the ground the same way. rooms: words in an area's name or id that a rule is kept to (straw only in a stable).
